newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Di Rupo cleared of child sex charges.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Di Rupo cleared of child sex charges.

text.p: A Belgian parliamentary commission, in a vote on Thursday, cleared Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo of allegations he had sex with under-age boys.

"The commission...considers that in the present state of the reports sent to parliament there are no indications of guilt and therefore no elements that would justify his indictment," commission chairman Raymond Langendries told reporters.
The 7-4 vote has to be endorsed by the full parliament.
But the vote after three days and nights of bitter debate, which revealed strains within the centre-left coalition, immediately triggered opposition charges of a cover-up.
"This is an exclusively political decision," said Didier Reynders, a member of the opposition Francophone Liberals. "This is not what the population expected."

An opinion poll, to be published in Friday's edition of populist paper La Derniere Heure, found almost three-quarters of those polled agreed with the commission's finding. Support was largest in Di Rupo's native Wallonia region.
At the same time, the commission approved a draft law simplifying parliamentary procedures for dealing with allegations against ministers and ex-ministers.

The new law aims would allow the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, to investigate allegations against ministers without having first to consult parliament. The court still needs parliamentary approval to indict or arrest a minister.

The Di Rupo case undermined public confidence in Belgium's establishment already shaken by a child sex and murder scandal that erupted last August. Child rapist Marc Dutroux was arrested in that affair and subsequently the bodies of four young girls weere discovered and two others rescued.

"This is a well-balanced decision which restores the honour of someone who has been haunted by unacceptable allegations," said Serge Moureaux, a member of the Francophone Socialists who together with their Flemish counterparts and the Dutch- and French-speaking Christian Democrats form the government.
The new law however means that the Di Rupo, number two in the government, could be investigated if any further allegations emerged.

He has already been cleared of allegations in one case file that he had sex with boys under the legal age of consent of 16 years. He denied the mostly anonymous charges in two other files that were handed to the commission on Monday.
